title: minimax-theorem-lean
abstract: A Lean formalization of von Neumann's 1928 finite two-player zero-sum minimax theorem, a foundation of modern game theory and a cornerstone of mathematical economics. Nash equilibrium existence builds directly on its mixed-strategy solution concept by extending equilibrium existence beyond the two-player zero-sum case; this is historical motivation, not a claimed Lean proof of Nash's theorem. The formal result is Minimax.minimax_theorem {A B : Type*} [Fintype A] [Fintype B] [Nonempty A] [Nonempty B] (u : A → B → ℝ) : maxminValue u = minmaxValue u. The reported Palomar registry API search on 2026-09-29 for "minimax" returned zero entries. The M1 Mathlib survey found no finite zero-sum game specialization in the pinned Mathlib, whose general Sion saddle-point theorem is reused here.
